cards.title: Fry the paste first
cards.body: Doubanjiang tastes raw until it meets hot oil. Fry it alone until the oil runs red, then build the sauce on that.
cards.tryTonight: Fry a spoonful of any chili paste before the stock goes in.

cards.title: The litchi balance
cards.body: Kung pao is sweet and sour before it is hot. Sugar and black vinegar pull against each other, and the scorched chilies sit on top.
cards.rule: Sugar and vinegar in about equal measure.
cards.tryTonight: Taste the sauce before it hits the wok: sweet and sour should arrive together.

cards.title: No fish in fish-fragrant
cards.body: The name is the seasoning once used for fish: pickled chili, garlic, ginger, scallion, sugar and vinegar. All three aromatics go in, and plenty of them.
cards.rule: Garlic, ginger and scallion, all three.
cards.tryTonight: Use the same six on pork slivers or tofu.

cards.title: Dress the bowl, not the pot
cards.body: The sauce is built in the bottom of the bowl: chili oil, soy and ground peppercorn. Hot noodles go on top and are tossed at the table.
cards.rule: Sauce in the bowl first, noodles second.
cards.tryTonight: Stir chili oil and soy in a bowl, then drop plain noodles on it.

cards.title: Cook it twice
cards.body: The belly is simmered whole, cooled and sliced, then fried until the slices curl and give up their fat. Only then does the bean paste go in.
cards.rule: Boil first, fry second, no added liquid.
cards.tryTonight: Fry leftover boiled or roast pork until the edges curl.

cards.title: Dry means no water
cards.body: The beans fry in oil until they wrinkle and blister. Nothing wet goes in, so the flavour concentrates and the seasonings cling.
cards.tryTonight: Fry green beans in a little oil until wrinkled before adding anything else.

cards.title: The oil comes last
cards.body: The fish poaches gently in a bean-paste broth. Then chilies and peppercorn are piled on top and smoking oil is poured over them. That is where the aroma comes from.
cards.tryTonight: Pour a spoonful of very hot oil over chili flakes on any soup.

cards.title: A cold dish, a loud dressing
cards.body: The chicken is poached and cooled, never fried. All the force is in the dressing: chili oil, soy, black vinegar, a little sugar and ground peppercorn.
cards.rule: Cook the chicken plain; season the sauce.
cards.tryTonight: Spoon chili oil, soy and vinegar over cold leftover chicken.

cards.title: Hunt for the chicken
cards.body: The chicken is fried crisp and buried in dried chilies. They perfume the oil and are mostly left on the plate.
cards.rule: Chilies for fragrance, not for eating.
cards.tryTonight: Toast a few whole dried chilies in the oil before you fry anything.

cards.title: Let the noodles drink
cards.body: Glass noodles soak up whatever they sit in. Braise them in the seasoned liquid until it is nearly gone and the pork clings like ants on twigs.
cards.rule: Cook until the liquid is absorbed, not drained.
cards.tryTonight: Finish any noodle in its sauce instead of in water.
